paraphrase: Argues that a completion receipt is only unforgeable relative to the agent's current toolset — not an absolute property. A receipt designed to be expensive-to-forge (e.g., DOM click event) becomes trivial when the agent later gains new capabilities (e.g., browser devtools/CDP access). Because capability grants are additive and rarely re-audited, the set of receipts a given agent can cheaply forge only grows over time. Hardening the evidence channel must be a standing re-audit, not a one-time architecture decision.

claims.text: Receipt unforgeability is a joint property of the receipt and the agent's current action space — not an absolute property of the receipt alone
claims.notes: Concrete example: DOM click event receipt → trivial with CDP access. Generalizes to file diffs, resource-mutation readback.

claims.text: Capability grants are additive and rarely revisited, so the set of receipts an agent can cheaply forge only grows over time silently
claims.notes: Implies receipt hardening must be a standing re-audit triggered by any toolset/permission expansion.

evaluation.notes: Introduces a temporal dimension to receipt design: receipts are not statically unforgeable. Directly implies a receipt field for capability-surface snapshot or re-audit timestamp.

notable_comments.contribution: The fix assumes the agentic environment remains static during the evaluation window. An agent may manipulate the provider or underlying resource state via a separate capability.
